newsitem.title: UK: No need now for international force - Rwanda leader.
newsitem.headline: No need now for international force - Rwanda leader.

text.p: Rwandan President Pasteur Bizimungu said on Friday he would tell the United Nations an international humanitarian force was no longer needed in eastern Zaire now that Hutu refugees were heading back into his country.

"The money which would have been devoted to the international force should be utilised for humanitarian assistance," Bizimungu told BBC television from the border town of Gisenye in what the network said was an exclusive interview.

Bizimungu said the force had been due to have a twofold mission -- to set up a corridor to get aid to the refugees and to separate them from Hutu militias. The corridor now was open and the separation had occurred, he added.

"Our country has been totally destroyed, the economy shattered, so we need that the international community make efforts to help us achieve mimimal economic conditions conducive to reconciliation," he said.

The United Nations Security Council agreed during private consultations on Friday on a resolution to deploy a Canadian-led multinational force to help refugees in eastern Zaire and it would be adopted later in the day, British U.N. envoy Sir John Weston said.

The mission of the force, eventually expected to number around 10,000, will be to help Rwandan Hutu refugees who fled to eastern Zaire in 1994 after the massacre in Rwanda of a million people, mainly rival Tutsis.
